reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's Leap and Creep (Book I); the frame (the jackal Victor telling the lion Rusty) and the verses are dropped, both disclosed.
Caste references (the guest verse and the flea's list of castes) are removed and disclosed; Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma are omitted with the Muladeva verse.

Age band 12+: the innocent louse host and its family are killed in one calm sentence while the guilty flea escapes. Fixed before approval: the content note no longer says the king is drawn lying down, and the king calls his servants in the plural.
The pause question comes before the bite; insects in the neuter; no em dashes.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, 321 KB; seams measured exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; painted to every edge with no text. The uneven generated rows were refitted by uniform scaling and cropping (bottom row cropped unscaled), never stretched, as the credit line says; heads stay in frame.
One edit pass replaced the middle-left panel so the flea bows low, fully in frame. The louse and flea are consistent and drawn cute rather than creepy; no dead insect, bite or blood is drawn.
The king and servants are fully clothed with similar skin tones and no caste markers.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels, not in the app in dark mode.
